Core reaches zero: 2324 measured -> 2307, all seventeen of them in odoo/addons.

    8  test_orm/views/test_orm_views.xml
    4  test_testing_utilities/views/menu.xml
    3  test_translation_import/data/test_translation_import_data.xml
    1  test_access_rights/data.xml
    1  test_translation_import/view.xml

`_sort_xml_records.py odoo/addons` fixed all five files; `_pretty_xml.py odoo/addons` then re-canonicalised the four the sort had reflowed, because the sorter collapses a multi-line element and the formatter owns the wrapping. Skipping that second pass is what a first attempt did, and `lint_xml_unformatted` went 3270 -> 3274 for it -- the two fixers have to be run as a pair over the same files, and both are idempotent afterwards (0 would change, 90 unchanged, each).

THE FLOOR OF 2320 WAS NEVER TRUE OF ANY TREE. It is banked here at what the tree measures rather than at what the previous floor claimed, and the difference is not a regression someone introduced:

    96e1eb3224f    banked 2320, note: "1fcc3d5f7d2 banked 2321 ... The tree measured 2320"
    the same tree  measures 2324, scanned with the linter own helpers
    HEAD           measures 2324, from the real test_lint run at the CI scope
    diff of the two violation SETS: 0 added, 0 removed

So nothing moved between those commits, in either direction, and the number banked at each of them was four below what was there. `96e1eb3224f` is the commit that fixed five floors of exactly this shape; this is the sixth, and it was introduced by the same measurement rather than found by it. The lesson its own note draws holds here: measure the tree at the commit that banks the floor.

Verified at the CI scope, `--addons-path=odoo/addons,addons -i test_lint`.
